_doc: Where the native iPhone rewrite stands, stage by stage. Read live by JatBot OS > Status > Jacked (agent repo scripts/project-pages.json, sources iosLocal/iosRemote; parser frontend/src/jatbot/projectPages.ts iosRewrite()). Any job that moves a stage updates THIS file in the same commit: set status, edit summary/detail, add commits, bump updated (ISO time with offset; the page shows whichever of the working-tree and origin/main copies has the later updated). status: done | gate (blocked on Mr. Roni, his turn) | active (being built now) | todo. Order = build order (IOS_REWRITE_PLAN.md 'Build order'). Plain words only: this text is shown to Mr. Roni as is.

stages.title: Kickoff and first screen
stages.summary: Xcode project with the login and sign-up screen, written on the desktop.
detail: Login and sign-up in Jacked's dark and teal look, session kept in the Keychain, a placeholder signed-in screen that reads your own profile to prove the login works.
Talks to Supabase with plain web calls, no extra package.
The networking part compiles on the desktop and passes 16 of 16 live read-only checks (re-run 2026-11-04 evening).
The screens and the Xcode project file have only been read through, never built in Xcode.

stages.title: Decisions locked
stages.summary: iOS 17 and up, one App Store listing with the watch app, plain web calls.
detail: Oldest supported: iOS 17, iPhone XS and newer.
One App Store listing for the iPhone app and Phil's Apple Watch app. The bundle id and team in the project are still a placeholder.
Plain web calls to Supabase, not the supabase-swift package (your final answer, twice).
Account deletion waits until the basics below work.

stages.title: First build in Xcode
stages.summary: Builds in Xcode on the Mac and runs in the iPhone simulator.
detail: Built with a real xcodebuild on the Mac and run in the simulator on 2026-11-06; screenshot and video were sent to you.
Agent jobs now build and screenshot it on the Mac themselves, signed in as a throwaway test account, never yours.

stages.title: Your workout history on the Home screen
stages.summary: Read-only: workout history, streak and calendar on the iPhone Home screen, plus the tab bar.
detail: Signs in, downloads the saved data and keeps a copy on the phone, one copy per account, so it opens offline.
Home shows the streak box, the month calendar (tap a day to see what was trained), Start Workout and the last 6 workouts; tap one for every exercise and set.
Checked in the iPhone simulator next to the web app, both signed in to the same throwaway test account: same streak, same best, same trained days, same workouts.
Writes nothing yet. Start Workout says logging is the next step.
Not on Home yet: the monthly recap card (comes with Metrics), the Suggested today card (comes with routines), the Gym years view.

stages.title: Safe saving
stages.summary: The careful save layer is in: the iPhone can rename a past workout and the web app shows it.
detail: Every save reads the latest copy from the server first, merges it with what's on the phone using the same rules as the web app, and only writes if nobody else saved in between. If someone did, it reads again and merges again.
The merge rules are a direct copy of the web app's. Checked on the Mac: 2,014 sample cases run through both the web app's code and the iPhone's code gave the same result every time.
Checked for real in the iPhone simulator on the throwaway test account: renamed a workout, the web app shows the new name, nothing else in the account changed.
Also forced the worst case: another device saved a workout while the iPhone was mid-save. Both the other workout and the iPhone's rename survived.
If the phone is offline, the change stays on the phone and goes out on the next sync.
Not yet: updating the friends leaderboard numbers after a save. That needs the stats math, which comes with workout logging and Metrics.

stages.title: Workout logging
stages.summary: Logging works like the web app: the iPhone logged workouts on the throwaway test account and the web app shows the same sets, volume and PRs.
detail: Start an empty workout, one of your routines, or a past day from the calendar ("Log a workout for this day"). Starting a new one while another is open asks first, like the web app.
On each exercise: weight and reps, check sets off, the greyed numbers from last time, a PREV column, add and remove sets, the rest timer with -15/+15/skip, the plate calculator.
Same buttons as the web app: Single/Both for one-arm lifts, Bodyweight/+ Added/- Assist for pull-ups and dips, Sec/Min/Hr for holds, miles and stopwatch-style minutes with the pace for runs.
Switch an exercise, pair two as a superset, reorder them, and a note per exercise that's remembered next time (saved through the careful save layer, the web app showed it).
One gold star per exercise on the record set, plus PR, Go up and Lighter badges, exactly the web app's rules. The finish summary shows new and suggested PRs and the moved-up / consider-lighter notes.

Checked side by side in the iPhone simulator and the web app, same test account: the same stars, badges, totals and pace, and finished workouts show up in the web app with the same sets, volume and PRs.
The finish math is copied from the web app and checked on the Mac: 600 of 600 random workouts came out identical.
Not checked: the Apple Watch, since no watch is attached to the simulator. The watch reads the same saved data the web app does.
Moved to the next step, because they need the muscle-group and stats math that comes with Metrics: the Suggested today card on Home and updating your leaderboard numbers after a save.

stages.title: Library, stats and friends
stages.summary: Done: every screen of the web app is on the iPhone, checked side by side on the throwaway test account. Last piece: Import (a Jacked backup or a Hevy file).
detail: Library done: search, the muscle chips, favourites first then what you've used, the PR on each row, and the exercise page with photos, your suggested PR, recent top weights and the how-to steps. Favourite, hide and create a custom exercise all save through the careful save layer.
Routines done: your routines in their sections like the web app, new, edit and delete a routine (it files itself into a section the same way), and Trusted Programs with + Add to Routines.

Metrics done: Overview, Body Weight (log today's weight, the trend line), the Muscle Map rankings with the how-it's-scored page, Workout Summary, Lifetime Stats with your top PR, and Monthly Recaps with the full recap page. Hide a card, reorder the cards and bring hidden ones back, like the web app.
Home now shows the monthly recap card on the 1st to the 7th of each month, until you close it.
The stats math is copied from the web app and checked on the Mac: 300 of 300 random accounts gave the same numbers on both sides, muscle rankings included.

Checked side by side on the throwaway test account: every number on every Metrics card matched the web app, and the muscle ranking order and levels were identical. A weight logged and a card hidden on the iPhone showed up in the web app.

Badges done: the Achievements card on Metrics (badges earned out of the total), the full list with the Jacked box on top and the Monthly, 3-month and Permanent groups, and each badge's own page with how to earn it, the Bronze, Silver and Gold ladder with "You" on your tier, which lift reached which tier, and your highest ever.
The badge math is copied from the web app and checked on the Mac: 300 of 300 random accounts gave the same badges, tiers, ladders and wording on both sides.

Checked side by side on the throwaway test account: every badge line on the iPhone matched the web app (Bench Bronze, Cardio Bronze at 8:17 a mile, this month's challenge Triceps 0 of 4, and the rest locked with the same numbers).
This month's Challenge muscle is saved the same way the web app saves it, through the careful save layer, so both always show the same one.
Small web app quirk, not copied: the web app's weight chart shows each date one day early (Oct 26 for an Oct 27 entry). The iPhone shows the real date.

Friends done: the friends list, add / accept / remove and close buddies, the leaderboards, a friend's profile with their stats, calendar and last 30 days of workouts down to every set, their badges, and Copy to my workout. Checked between two throwaway accounts: the friends list, the this-month weight and all-time PR boards, the friend's profile, workout and badges, and the copied workout all matched the web app.

Suggested today on Home: the same three muscle groups with the same days-since, the same trusted pick of the day, and each Start button builds the same workout as the web app (checked all four on the test account). Closing the card hides it on the web app too.
Gym years: tap the month name on Home (or Gym years on a friend's profile) for every trained day, one square per day. Same squares lit as the web app.
The calendar day view now shows the gold PR lines (the exercise with a star and the record set), matching the web app on every test day.
Your leaderboard numbers update after every saved workout: logged one on the test account, and the friend account saw 19 workouts straight away.

Routines: Today's pick is marked on Trusted Programs, a section folds away when you tap its name, a long press renames it, and Reorder moves sections and the routines inside them, plus + Section. All of it showed the same in the web app.

Exercise page: Edit (the full form for your own exercises, name, category, equipment, notes and assist for built-in ones), Reset PR with the web app's warning, and a photo for your own exercises that stays on the phone, like the web app's.

Monthly recap: the tiered badge grid, the Leaderboard crown when you topped last month, and Share, which sends the recap as a picture with a one-line caption. The October recap matched the web app line for line.
Muscle Map now has the front and back body drawing, coloured by the same strength levels. It uses the web app's own artwork, and the colours matched region for region on the test account.
Monthly Recaps list: the crown next to last month when you topped your board. October 2026 shows it on both sides.
Badge pages: the dumbbell and Smith machine sections on Bench, the dumbbell section on Shoulder and the two run types on Cardio, with the web app's exact words.
Badge pages: tap a tier you reached, or Highest ever, to see the exact set that earned it. Bench and Cardio showed the same date, exercise and numbers as the web app.

Badge pages: the start button (Start a bench workout, Start a big-3 workout, Train your challenge muscle now, and so on). It picks the same exercises as the web app, and adds them to an open workout if you already have one.

Gold PR lines on old workouts saved before the app kept a PR record: worked out by replaying your whole history like the web app. Checked on the Mac: 300 of 300 random histories gave the same stars. On the test account both apps show the count only on those days, because the saved count there disagrees with the replay.
A past workout can be saved as a routine. The web app showed the new routine.

Edit Workout and Delete Workout on a past workout: name, date, every set's numbers and check, add or remove a set, remove an exercise, or delete the whole workout (behind the ... button, with the web app's confirm). Both rebuild your records for the exercises they touch, the same way the web app does. Checked on the Mac: 300 of 300 random edits and deletes gave the same history and records as the web app's own code.

Fixed first, from the second-opinion review: an iPhone edit to an old workout could be undone by the web app's next save. Every edit (renames too) now marks the workout as the newer version. Checked for real on the test account with the web app already open and holding its own older copy: the iPhone changed a set to 66 lb x 6, the web app then finished a workout and saved, and the iPhone and the server both still had 66 lb x 6. A delete on the iPhone also stuck and removed that workout's record.

Known and not fixable from the iPhone alone: settings, routines, profile, favourites and hidden cards are saved as a whole, so a change made on one app can be undone by the other app's next save while both are in use.

Edit Workout can now add an exercise you forgot (+ Add Exercise, its first set already ticked, the same one twice is refused). Checked on the test account: Hammer Curls added to a past workout on the iPhone, and the web app showed the same 2 sets, 661 lb and the new Hammer Curls record with its star.

Profile photo: Add Photo, or Edit Photo with Edit and Delete behind it, like the web app. The picture is cropped square and small before upload. Checked on the test account: the web app showed the iPhone's photo, and Delete removed it on both sides.

Username change on My Profile: refuses one that's taken, then moves the account, its saved data and its friend links to the new name in one server step. Checked on the test account: changed it, signed in again by the new name with all 19 workouts there, then changed it back.

Import on My Profile: a Jacked backup file or a Hevy CSV export (Strong-style files too), with the web app's same questions (replace your data? pounds or kilograms?). The import math is copied from the web app and checked on the Mac: 660 of 660 random files and dates gave the same result on both sides, exercise matching included. Checked on the test account: a Hevy file with a push day, a run and a leg day came in exactly as the web app would save it, same sets, records and stars on the day view; importing it again added nothing; a backup file with one extra workout added it and the web app showed it.

stages.title: Settings and account deletion
stages.summary: Built and live. Delete Account really deletes the account now.
detail: My Profile works like the web app: name, units, default rest, rep range, auto rest timer, your username with Copy (and changing it), your photo, and Body Metrics (body, body weight, birthday with your age). Saved through the careful save layer; the web app showed the same values after an iPhone save on the test account.
Also on Profile: Export a backup file, Sync now, add or change the email on file, Sign Out.
Delete Account (Apple requires it): a warning page, type your username to confirm, then Delete. The app then signs out.

The server side is live: it works out whose account it is from the signed-in session only, refuses if the typed username isn't yours, then removes your saved workouts, their history copies, every friendship and friend request, your photo, your profile and finally the login itself. If a step fails it stops and says so instead of claiming it worked.

Tested for real on throwaway accounts made just for this, never yours or the shared test account: the wrong username and a signed-out call were refused with nothing touched; the right one removed everything, the login stopped working, and the other two accounts and their own friend request were untouched.
Checked in the simulator on a fourth throwaway account: the real Delete button deleted it on the server and the app went back to the Log in screen.

stages.title: Look and feel matched to the web app
stages.summary: The iPhone app now looks like the web app: same fonts, same line icons, same floating bottom bar, same glowing teal buttons, same photo fallbacks.
detail: Text is DM Sans and the headings Barlow Condensed, bundled in the app (400/500/600 and 300), the same fonts the web app loads.

All the web app's own line icons (the 34 in its icon set, the five tab icons, close, check, play, eye) are bundled as vector images and used instead of Apple's symbols wherever the web app has its own. Apple symbols stay only for a few controls the web app draws with plain text characters (the + signs, the right arrows, the plate calculator ring).
The bottom bar is the web app's floating frosted capsule with the sliding teal pill; labels are small capitals. Primary buttons have the same teal gradient and glow.
Exercise photos that cannot load show the web app's dumbbell (heart for cardio) line icon tinted by muscle colour. Photos are kept on the phone after first load, so they show offline.
Added the pieces that were missing: tapping a friend's profile photo enlarges it, Send Feedback in My Profile, and the web app's haptic taps (tab change, set ticked, rest over, Single/Both).
The app icon was compared to the web app's 512px icon pixel by pixel: identical.

Not on the iPhone: the phone-and-watch shared live workout (that is the Apple Watch stage below), invite links that open the app directly (needs an Apple-hosted link file, see the blocker list), and the 'save to cloud?' prompt (not applicable: the iPhone app saves to your account from the first workout).

stages.title: iPhone-only extras and the watch
stages.summary: Rest timer on the Lock Screen, Apple Health, Face ID, live workout with the Apple Watch.
detail: At least one real native feature helps with Apple's review and is the reason to have an app at all.
Apple Health is also the smart-scale path you asked about.

stages.title: App Store paperwork
stages.summary: Privacy policy, privacy labels, screenshots, age rating, trademark check on the name Jacked.
detail: The trademark check is better done early: renaming after launch is expensive.
Privacy labels must match what the app really collects: username, optional email, workouts, body weight, birthday, sex, photo.

stages.title: Submit to the App Store
detail: Needs everything above.
The signing team and final bundle id, the upload and the review are steps only you can do on the Mac and in App Store Connect.
